children: Meesho shares jumped up to 12 per cent in Tuesday's trading session after brokerage firm UBS raised its target price on the stock, marking the biggest single-day gain in the last three months.

UBS maintained its "buy" recommendation on Meesho and raised its target price to Rs 260 per share from Rs 210 apiece. The revised target indicates an upside potential of 18.6 per cent from the previous closing price.

"We value Meesho using a combination of DCF and multiples. On the multiples approach, we apply a 40x EV/EBITDA multiple (unchanged) on 3YF EBITDA, i.e. average of FY30-31, and discount it back by two years, deriving a PT of Rs 260," UBS said.

While its FY27 estimates are largely unchanged, UBS raised its FY29-31 NMV estimates by 7-18 per cent, with a similar increase in contribution profit estimates and a 20-40 per cent increase in EBITDA estimates.

"Higher NMV forecasts reflect the continued flywheel from sellers (+81 per cent YoY to 1.04 million in Q1FY27), buyers (+29 per cent YoY to 274 million), coupled with rapid expansion in SKUs and logistics partners," it said.
The brokerage said the larger increase in EBITDA estimates reflects a stronger medium-term margin trajectory, driven by improving ads monetisation and logistics economics.

Management remains confident in the FY27 growth outlook. Although the shift in Diwali from October 2025 to November 2026 should result in slower growth in Q2 and faster growth in Q3, low-30s NMV growth remains achievable for FY27, UBS said.

Meesho expects around 25 per cent NMV CAGR over FY26-31, given substantial runway in both new customers and increased frequency. The company targets more than 500 million annual transacting users (ATUs) in the medium term, almost twice the 274 million ATUs as of Q1FY27.
The ordering frequency of the oldest user cohorts, on the platform for more than five years, is 20 times the platform average of 10 times and new-user frequency of 6-7 times.
Recently acquired users have also shown strong promise, with cohorts of more than three years showing 15 times frequency, while each cohort continues to increase usage.

Around 50-55 per cent of new users are organic, and dropout among users who use the platform three to four times tends to be low, resulting in an 18-month payback period for new-user acquisition, UBS said.
"These assumptions require logistics costs to continue declining and AOVs to fall at a mid-single-digit rate annually, bringing new customers and use cases onto the ecosystem," it added.

title: Meesho shares jump 12% as UBS sees up to 19% upside; stock near its post-listing high
